cls: Synthetic steroid with estrogenic, progestogenic and weak androgenic activity (tissue-selective)
pharm: Menopausal hormone therapy (STEAR - selective tissue estrogenic activity regulator)
quick: May be taken with or without food, at the same time each day
Contraindicated - not for use in pregnancy
Breast exam/mammography, BP, endometrial/vaginal bleeding, lipids
summary: Tibolone is a synthetic steroid whose metabolites have estrogenic, progestogenic and weak androgenic effects acting in a tissue-selective manner. It is used to treat estrogen-deficiency symptoms in postmenopausal women (at least 12 months after menopause) and to prevent osteoporosis in women at high fracture risk. It is not FDA-approved in the United States; this record follows EMA/SmPC and BNF data. Like other menopausal hormone therapy it increases risks of stroke, breast and endometrial cancer, and venous thromboembolism.
indications: Treatment of symptoms of estrogen deficiency in postmenopausal women (more than one year after menopause)
Prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk of fracture who are intolerant of, or contraindicated for, other agents

dosage.n: One tablet daily; no fixed end date but review periodically
Start the day after completing the previous regimen

admin: Take one tablet daily, swallowed whole with water, preferably at the same time each day
Should only be started at least 12 months after the last natural menstrual period
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals
Adequate dietary calcium and vitamin D when used for osteoporosis
moa: Tibolone is rapidly metabolized to three active compounds: two estrogenic metabolites (3-alpha- and 3-beta-hydroxy-tibolone) and a delta-4 isomer with progestogenic and androgenic activity. Tissue-selective metabolism and enzyme regulation (e.g., sulfatase/sulfotransferase) produce estrogenic effects in bone, brain and vagina, while local conversion in the endometrium and breast favours progestogenic/androgenic activity, limiting endometrial and breast stimulation.

absolute: Known, past or suspected breast cancer
Known or suspected estrogen-dependent malignancy (e.g., endometrial cancer)
Previous or current venous thromboembolism (DVT, PE)
Active or recent arterial thromboembolic disease (angina, MI, stroke)
Active liver disease / abnormal liver function until normalized
relative: Risk factors for thromboembolism or estrogen-dependent tumours

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. If pregnancy occurs during treatment, tibolone should be stopped immediately. There is no indication for use in pregnancy and inadvertent exposure of a fetus is to be avoided.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is established; data in significant renal impairment are limited, so use with caution.
hepatic: Contraindicated in active liver disease or while liver function tests remain abnormal. Discontinue if cholestatic jaundice or clinically significant liver dysfunction occurs.

major: Anticoagulants/warfarin (tibolone may increase fibrinolytic activity and enhance anticoagulant effect - monitor INR)
moderate: Enzyme-inducing drugs (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital) reduce tibolone effect
St John's Wort (reduces efficacy via enzyme induction)
HIV protease inhibitors / NNRTIs (variable enzyme effects)
interactions.food: Grapefruit juice has limited relevance; no major food interaction
interactions.diagnostics: May affect thyroid and other binding proteins and lipid measurements

serious: Increased risk of endometrial cancer / hyperplasia

monitoring: Regular breast examination and mammography per screening guidance
Investigation of any unexpected or persistent vaginal bleeding
Liver function if symptoms suggest dysfunction
Periodic reassessment of benefit/risk of continued therapy
counsel: Report any unexpected vaginal bleeding, especially after the first months
Perform regular breast self-checks and attend mammography screening
Seek urgent care for sudden severe headache, weakness, chest pain, breathlessness, or leg swelling/pain
Take at the same time each day; this is not a contraceptive
Discuss the small increased risks of breast cancer, stroke and clots with your doctor
pk: Symptom relief develops over several weeks of daily dosing
Active metabolites peak within ~1.5-4 hours of an oral dose
Approximately 7-8 hours for the active hydroxy metabolites
Store below 25-30 C in original packaging; protect from moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved in the US; this record is based on EMA/SmPC and BNF sources
STEAR with combined estrogenic, progestogenic and weak androgenic actions - a single agent for menopausal HRT without separate progestogen
Should be started at least 12 months after the last menstrual period to limit irregular bleeding
Carries menopausal-hormone-therapy risks: breast/endometrial cancer, stroke and VTE - use lowest effective dose for shortest time
May reduce HDL and triglycerides via its androgenic metabolite
missed: If a dose is missed and it is within about 12 hours of the usual time, take it as soon as remembered. If more than 12 hours have passed, skip the missed tablet and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not take two tablets together. Missed doses may increase breakthrough bleeding.
overdose: Acute toxicity is low. Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting and, in women, vaginal bleeding. No specific antidote exists; management is symptomatic and supportive.
